districts.name: Thiruvananthapuram
districts.description: The capital city, blending culture, history and coastal beauty.

places.name: Kovalam Beach
places.description: Kovalam is an internationally renowned beach destination with a naturally defined bay of three beaches. The crescent-shaped beach with a rock promontory offers crystal clear water, safe swimming and excellent sunbathing. The iconic Vizhinjam Lighthouse stands tall overlooking the turquoise Arabian Sea.

places.name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple
places.description: One of the 108 Divya Desams dedicated to Lord Vishnu, this temple is known for its unique Dravidian architecture and the vast treasure discovered in its vaults. The deity Padmanabhaswamy is depicted in the Anantha Shayana posture (reclining on the serpent Anantha).

places.name: Varkala Beach
places.description: Varkala is unique among Kerala beaches for the cliffs adjacent to the Arabian Sea. Known as Papanasam Beach, the mineral springs that flow onto the beach are believed to have holy properties. The cliff-top promenade lined with cafes and shops is a highlight.

places.name: Napier Museum
places.description: A stunning Indo-Saracenic styled museum housing an eclectic collection of bronze idols, ancient ornaments, ivory carvings, and temple chariots. The building itself is an architectural marvel designed by Robert Fellowes Chisholm.

places.name: Agasthyarkoodam
places.description: The second highest peak in Kerala, Agasthyarkoodam (1868m) is a trekker's paradise known for its rare medicinal plants and rich biodiversity. The peak is named after sage Agasthya and is considered sacred.

places.name: Kuthiramalika Palace Museum
places.description: A stunning 19th-century palace built by Maharaja Swathi Thirunal with 122 horse sculptures adorning the walls. The palace houses royal artifacts, paintings and an antique collection.

places.name: Ponmudi Hill Station
places.description: A scenic hill station at 1067m altitude surrounded by tea gardens and dense forests. Known for its winding ghat roads with 22 hairpin bends and stunning valley views.

places.name: Shanghumugham Beach
places.description: A popular city beach near Trivandrum Airport with a giant mermaid sculpture, aquarium, and a beautiful sunset view. Ideal for evening walks.

places.name: Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary
places.description: Home to a lion safari park, crocodile farm, deer park and the scenic Neyyar Dam. Trek through dense forests to spot elephants, leopards and over 200 bird species.

places.name: Neyyar Dam & Wildlife Sanctuary
places.description: A hidden gem nestled in the Western Ghats, the Neyyar Dam is surrounded by dense forest and forms the core of the Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary. Home to lion-tailed macaques, elephants and leopards, this serene reservoir offers boating and crocodile-watching that very few tourists know about.

places.name: Poovar Island
places.description: A secluded island at the confluence of the Neyyar River and the Arabian Sea, accessible only by boat. Poovar is one of Kerala's most secret escapes — golden sand beaches, backwater lagoons fringed with coconut palms, and no motor vehicles.

places.name: Agasthyakoodam Peak
places.description: The second highest peak in Kerala at 1868m, Agasthyakoodam is shrouded in mystery and biodiversity. Access is restricted to protect rare medicinal plants; guided treks are permitted only from January to March. An extraordinary secret for serious trekkers.

places.name: Vizhinjam Juma Masjid
places.description: One of the oldest mosques on the Malabar Coast, dating back to the 8th century. Built with ancient stone and coral, this hidden heritage site near the fishing harbour is rarely visited but deeply significant in Kerala's Islamic history.

places.name: Bonacaud Estate
places.description: A colonial-era tea and rubber estate hidden deep in the hills near Thiruvananthapuram. Former British rest house surrounded by misty valleys, waterfall streams and untouched jungle. Virtually unknown to mainstream tourists.

places.name: Akkulam Tourist Village
places.description: A beautiful freshwater lake on the outskirts of the city, Akkulam is a local favourite for boating and picnics. The adjoining tourist village has a small water park, swimming pool, and children's park — perfect for families.

places.name: Kuthiramalika (Puthenmalika) Palace
places.description: A 19th-century palace built by Maharaja Swathi Thirunal, famed for its magnificent wooden architecture featuring 122 horse sculptures carved under the eaves. The palace houses a museum of royal artefacts, ivory carvings, and paintings.

places.name: Kadinamkulam Lake
places.description: A pristine coastal lake separated from the sea by a narrow strip of land, offering stunning views and calm backwaters. Almost completely unknown to tourists, frequented only by local fishermen and migratory birds.

places.name: Aruvikkara Dam & Nature Reserve
places.description: A serene dam on the Karamana River forming the main drinking water reservoir for Thiruvananthapuram city. The surrounding forest is a protected nature reserve with crocodiles, monitor lizards and migratory birds. Very few tourists make the trip here.

places.name: Veli Tourist Village & Lagoon
places.description: A picturesque spot where the Veli Lake meets the Arabian Sea, connected by a narrow land strip. The floating bridge, water scooters, children's park and stunning sunset views make it a beloved local escape rarely on tourist maps.

places.name: Aazhimala Shiva Temple & Beach
places.description: A dramatic cliffside Shiva temple overlooking the Arabian Sea, with a massive statue of Lord Shiva emerging from the waves. The temple is carved into the rocky coastline and the adjacent beach remains pristine and largely unknown.

places.name: Anchuthengu Fort (Anjengo Fort)
places.description: One of the oldest and least-visited British forts in India, built in 1696. The partially ruined fort stands on a thin strip of land between the backwaters and the sea. The old British cemetery and lighthouse ruins add eerie historical depth.

places.name: Sree Narayana Guru Sivagiri Mutt
places.description: The final resting place and spiritual headquarters of the great social reformer Sree Narayana Guru, set on a hilltop overlooking the sea. The Sivagiri Pilgrimage (December 30–January 1) draws 500,000 pilgrims and is one of South India's most peaceful mass gatherings.

places.name: Kottukal Cave Temple
places.description: A rare rock-cut cave temple dating back to the Pallava period, buried deep in the forest near Thiruvananthapuram. The sculptures inside rival those of Mahabalipuram but remain almost entirely unvisited due to difficult access.

places.name: Priyadarshini Planetarium
places.description: One of South India's premier planetariums located in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, featuring state-of-the-art dome shows on astronomy, space exploration and the cosmos. Especially magical for children and astronomy enthusiasts.

places.name: Kavalayam Wetland Bird Sanctuary
places.description: A hidden Ramsar-recognised wetland on the outskirts of the city, providing critical habitat for over 100 species of birds including the painted stork, open-billed stork and spoonbill. Virtually no tourist infrastructure exists here.

places.name: Kowdiar Palace
places.description: The official residence of the Royal Family of Travancore, a stunning Indo-Saracenic palace rarely open to public view. The palace gardens and external architecture are visible from the road and the heritage significance is immense.

places.name: Government Science & Technology Museum
places.description: One of South India's finest science museums with interactive exhibits on physics, astronomy, geology and Kerala's traditional technology including ancient irrigation systems, ship-building and spice processing methods.

places.name: Parassala Backwater Trail
places.description: A hidden backwater circuit near the Tamil Nadu border with no tourist development whatsoever. The narrow canals passing through coconut groves and paddy fields are navigated only by traditional wooden boats owned by local fishermen.

places.name: Sarkara Devi Temple
places.description: An ancient and powerful Devi temple on a hilltop near Chirayinkeezhu, famously known for the first elephant of Padmanabhaswamy Temple receiving its ceremonial blessing here. The forest setting and ancient stone architecture are captivating.

places.name: Traditional Kerala Sadhya Experience
places.description: A Sadhya is a grand vegetarian feast of 26+ dishes served on a banana leaf, representing the pinnacle of Kerala's culinary tradition. Thiruvananthapuram's temple restaurants and heritage hotels offer the most authentic version of this centuries-old tradition.

places.name: East Fort Street Food Hub
places.description: The area around East Fort and Chalai Bazaar is Thiruvananthapuram's most vibrant street food zone. Kappa biryani (tapioca with beef), Kerala-style beef fry, puttu kadala curry, and freshly squeezed sugarcane juice are served all day in a lively market atmosphere.

places.name: Thiruvananthapuram Chaaya Kada (Tea Shop) Culture
places.description: The humble chaaya kada (tea shop) is the heartbeat of Thiruvananthapuram's social life. Kadala curry with porotta, unniyappam, pazham pori (banana fritter) and the distinctively thick, cardamom-infused Kerala chai make the local tea shop experience unmissable.

places.name: Edava-Nadayara Backwater Lake
places.description: A pristine coastal lake system in southern Thiruvananthapuram district, Edava-Nadayara is the meeting point of the Pamba River backwaters with the sea. Completely undeveloped, the vast shallow lake is a haven for flamingos, painted storks and thousands of migrating waders.

districts.name: Ernakulam (Kochi)
districts.description: The commercial capital, a cosmopolitan city known as the Queen of the Arabian Sea.

places.name: Fort Kochi
places.description: Fort Kochi is a historic neighbourhood with colonial-era architecture, art galleries, and the iconic Chinese fishing nets. A blend of Portuguese, Dutch, and British influences make it one of India's most unique heritage zones. The Mattancherry Palace and Jewish Synagogue are nearby.

places.name: Alleppey Backwaters (from Kochi)
places.description: The Venice of the East, Alleppey offers an enchanting network of lagoons, lakes, and rivers. A houseboat cruise through these tranquil backwaters is a quintessential Kerala experience with views of paddy fields, coconut groves, and village life.

places.name: Wonderla Amusement Park
places.description: One of South India's premier amusement parks featuring thrilling rides, water attractions, and live entertainment. Perfect for a fun-filled family day out.

places.name: Cherai Beach
places.description: Located on Vypeen Island, Cherai is a pristine 15km long beach where backwaters and sea waters coexist. Dolphins can sometimes be spotted. The beach has golden sands and clear waters perfect for swimming.

places.name: Hill Palace Museum
places.description: The largest archaeological museum in Kerala, Hill Palace was the official residence of Kochi's erstwhile royal family. Set across 52 acres, it houses royal memorabilia, paintings, and ancient artifacts.

places.name: Bolgatty Island
places.description: A historic island in the Vembanad backwaters housing the 18th-century Dutch-built Bolgatty Palace, now converted to a heritage hotel. Accessible only by boat.

places.name: Mangalavanam Bird Sanctuary
places.description: A rare mangrove forest and bird sanctuary right in the heart of Kochi city. Home to 187 species of birds and a crucial green lung of the city.

places.name: Jew Town & Mattancherry
places.description: A historic Jewish heritage zone with the famous Pardesi Synagogue (1568 AD), antique shops, spice warehouses, and the Dutch Palace with remarkable Kerala murals.

places.name: Vypeen Island
places.description: A long island accessible by ferry with pristine beaches, the historic Pallippuram Fort (1503 CE), and a relaxed fishing village atmosphere away from tourist crowds.

places.name: Bolghatty Island
places.description: A hidden island in Vembanad Lake accessible only by ferry, home to the historic Bolghatty Palace — once the residence of Dutch and British governors. The island exudes colonial charm with its overgrown gardens and heritage hotel.

places.name: Pilikode Secret Rock Beach
places.description: A virtually undiscovered rocky cove near Cherai, accessible through a fishing village. The dramatic black rocks, tidal pools and absence of crowds make it one of Kochi's best-kept secrets. Local fishermen are your only company.

places.name: Edakulam Organic Farm
places.description: A working organic farm and eco-resort hidden in the rolling countryside near Kochi. Offers farm-to-table experiences, bullock-cart rides, paddy field walks and traditional Kerala cooking classes. An authentic rural escape.

places.name: Vypeen Island & Lighthouse
places.description: Vypeen Island, connected to the mainland by ferry and bridge, hides a 200-year-old lighthouse and pristine beaches rarely visited by tourists. The island's old churches, Portuguese forts and quiet fishing villages are remarkable.

places.name: Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica
places.description: One of only eight basilicas in India, this stunning colonial cathedral in Fort Kochi was originally built by the Portuguese in 1558 and designated a basilica by Pope John Paul II. Its neo-Gothic façade and pastel interiors are breathtaking.

places.name: Kalvathy Backwater Village
places.description: A hidden network of narrow canals and coconut-fringed backwater villages on the outskirts of Kochi, completely bypassed by tourists. The local country boat rides through ancient Christian villages reveal a Kerala unchanged for centuries.

places.name: Paradesi Synagogue, Mattancherry
places.description: The oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth of Nations, built in 1568 in the Jew Town of Mattancherry. Its hand-painted Chinese floor tiles, Belgian crystal chandeliers and ancient Torah scrolls are extraordinary. Only a few dozen Jews remain in the congregation.

places.name: Willingdon Island
places.description: An artificial island created in the 1930s from material dredged out of Kochi harbour — the largest man-made island in India. Home to naval establishments, the original Taj Malabar hotel and a little-explored waterfront with spectacular harbour views.

places.name: Periyar River Heritage Cruise
places.description: A little-known river cruise on the lower Periyar River from Aluva to Kochi, passing through mangrove forests, ancient temples on the riverbanks and traditional fishing villages. The 3-hour journey offers a completely different perspective on Kochi.

places.name: Kaladi — Birthplace of Adi Shankaracharya
places.description: The sacred birthplace of Adi Shankaracharya, the 8th-century philosopher who unified Hinduism and established the Advaita Vedanta school. The riverside temples, gurukuls and the Sharada Peetham shrine draw scholars from across the world.

places.name: Kumbalangi Integrated Tourism Village
places.description: India's first model tourism village, Kumbalangi is a backwater island community that turned its traditional fishing practices into sustainable eco-tourism. Crab fishing, toddy tapping, coir making and mangrove kayaking are all authentic.

places.name: Thripunithura Vrischikotsavam Festival
places.description: The ancient royal town of Thripunithura hosts one of Kerala's most spectacular temple festivals with grand processions of 50+ caparisoned elephants during the Vrischikotsavam in November-December. The Hill Palace and ancient temples nearby complete the experience.

places.name: Cherai River Mouth Dolphin Cruise
places.description: At the northern tip of Vypeen Island, where the backwaters meet the sea at Cherai, spinner dolphins are regularly spotted in the early morning. Local fishermen offer informal boat rides at dawn — one of Kerala's most secret wildlife experiences.

places.name: Chendamangalam Heritage Village
places.description: A remarkable village hosting the ruins of three different civilizations — a Dutch fort, a 16th century synagogue and an ancient mosque — within 500 metres of each other. The village is barely known but represents the extraordinary multicultural history of Kochi.

places.name: Aluva Mahasivarathri Festival
places.description: The world's largest Sivaratri celebration, held on the sandy midstream island (Manappuram) of the Periyar River at Aluva. Half a million devotees worship through the night in the open air on this sacred sand island that appears only in winter.

places.name: Thattekkad Bird Sanctuary
places.description: Declared India's richest bird habitat by the great ornithologist Salim Ali, Thattekkad hosts 300+ species including rare endemics. The sanctuary sits in a loop of the Periyar River and the dawn chorus here is legendary among bird watchers.

places.name: Pizhala Island Village
places.description: A hidden island community in Vembanad Lake accessible only by ferry from Kochi. The island has no hotels, no shops and is home to a traditional toddy-tapping community. The backwater views from the island are extraordinary.

places.name: Fort Kochi Heritage Cafe Trail
places.description: Fort Kochi's colonial lanes are lined with heritage cafes serving a fusion of Kerala, Portuguese, Dutch and British culinary traditions. Duck curry, Syrian Christian stew, Malabar parotta and the famous Kochi prawn moilee in atmospheric heritage settings.

places.name: Mattancherry Spice Quarter & Food Trail
places.description: The historic spice warehouses and Jewish Quarter of Mattancherry form the backdrop for one of Kerala's most aromatic food trails. Pepper, cardamom, nutmeg, and cinnamon fill the air as you discover Syrian Jewish recipes, Cochin-style fish curry and the legendary Kochi prawn pickle.

places.name: Kochi Chinese Fishing Net Seafood Stalls
places.description: The most photogenic food experience in Kerala — buying freshly landed seafood at the Chinese fishing nets and having it cooked immediately at adjacent stalls. Grilled prawns, butter fish and spiced calamari cooked minutes after the catch makes this uniquely Kochi.

places.name: Kodungallur Backwater Trail
places.description: One of Kerala's oldest port cities, Kodungallur's backwaters were the entry point for all ancient maritime trade — Chinese, Arab, Jewish and Roman merchants all docked here. The heritage waterways passing ancient synagogues, mosque ruins and the Cheraman Masjid (India's first mosque) make this a uniquely historic backwater experience.

places.name: Cherai Beach & Backwater Confluence
places.description: Cherai is the rare place where backwater canals run parallel to the beach, separated by just a thin strip of land. Dolphins are regularly spotted offshore, while the canal side offers kayaking through coconut-fringed waterways. The unique beach-backwater combination is found nowhere else in Kerala.

districts.name: Idukki (Munnar)
districts.description: Kerala's high-range district with lush tea plantations, misty hills, and wildlife sanctuaries.

places.name: Munnar Tea Gardens
places.description: Munnar is home to some of the world's highest tea plantations, carpeting the hills in a sea of green. At 1600m above sea level, the cool climate and panoramic views of rolling hills draped in tea bushes make it a visual treat. Visit the Tea Museum to learn about tea processing.

places.name: Eravikulam National Park
places.description: Home to the endangered Nilgiri Tahr, this national park spans 97 sq km of rolling grasslands and shola forests. The park blooms spectacularly during Neelakurinji flowering (once every 12 years), turning entire hillsides blue-purple.

places.name: Mattupetty Dam
places.description: A scenic dam set amidst lush green forests and tea plantations at an altitude of 1700m. Boating on the reservoir offers stunning views of the surrounding hills. The nearby Indo-Swiss livestock project is also worth visiting.

places.name: Top Station
places.description: At 1868m, Top Station is one of the highest points in South India accessible by road. The misty views of the Western Ghats and the tea-covered valleys below are breathtaking. On clear days, the Tamil Nadu plains are visible.

places.name: Attukal Waterfalls
places.description: A series of cascading waterfalls cutting through thick cardamom and spice plantations. The trek to the falls passes through misty forests and is refreshing with the sound of rushing water echoing through the valley.

places.name: Rajamala (Eravikulam)
places.description: Core zone of Eravikulam National Park at 2695m altitude. The best place to see the endangered Nilgiri Tahr mountain goat up close. Also blooms with Neelakurinji every 12 years.

places.name: Lockhart Gap
places.description: A scenic mountain pass at 1500m offering dramatic valley views of tea plantations stretching to the horizon. Perfect photography spot for misty mornings.

places.name: Chinnakanal Waterfalls
places.description: A stunning 2000-foot waterfall cascading through misty forests, also called Power House Waterfalls. Surrounded by cardamom, pepper and coffee plantations.

places.name: Munnar Rose Garden
places.description: A colorful rose garden perched on a hilltop with 2000+ varieties of roses, ferns, cacti and orchids. Managed by DTPC, it is one of the most visited family attractions near Munnar.

places.name: Lakkam Waterfalls
places.description: A hidden waterfall deep inside the Rajamala forests, reachable via a narrow jungle trail known only to locals. The 50-ft cascade plunges into a crystal-clear pool surrounded by cardamom and shola forest. Almost no tourist infrastructure exists.

places.name: Chinnakanal Powerhouse Waterfalls
places.description: A stunning hidden waterfall near Chinnakanal village, descending in multiple tiers through lush cardamom estates. The approach involves crossing streams and trekking through private spice gardens — very few tourists venture here.

places.name: Kundala Lake & Dam
places.description: A serene high-altitude lake formed by the Kundala Dam surrounded by rolling tea estates and pine forests. The shikara boat rides on the lake with misty mountain backdrops and rose gardens make it exceptionally picturesque.

places.name: Pothamedu View Point
places.description: A breathtaking but relatively unknown viewpoint offering a panoramic view of Munnar's tea, coffee and cardamom plantations stretching to the horizon. The winding path through the plantations is itself a highlight.

places.name: Marayoor Sandalwood Forest
places.description: The only natural sandalwood forest in Kerala, Marayoor is a hidden gem 40 km from Munnar. The government-managed sandalwood forests here are the last remaining in South India. The area also has ancient Muniyara dolmens.

places.name: Kolukkumalai Tea Estate
places.description: The world's highest tea estate at 7900 ft above sea level, accessible only by jeep on treacherous mountain roads. Kolukkumalai produces some of the finest orthodox tea and offers one of the most dramatic sunrise views in India.

places.name: Anayirankal Dam & Reservoir
places.description: A hidden high-altitude reservoir deep in the Munnar forest, accessible via a narrow mountain road almost never shown in tourist guides. The surrounding pine and eucalyptus forests host Nilgiri Tahr and rare orchids.

places.name: Rajamala Wildlife Trail
places.description: Beyond the main Eravikulam NP area, the extended Rajamala trail leads through cloud forest to hidden viewpoints rarely visited. The misty grasslands and shola patches are home to Nilgiri Tahr, sambar and lion-tailed macaques.

places.name: Devikulam Hill Station
places.description: A serene hill station 15km from Munnar sitting at 1800m, named after the lake where the goddess Sita is said to have bathed. The Sita Devi Lake, rolling meadows and zero-tourist atmosphere make it the perfect Munnar escape from crowds.

places.name: Thoovanam Waterfall, Chinnakanal
places.description: A spectacular but completely unknown waterfall in the Pambar River gorge accessible via a forest trek. The name means 'spray of water' in Malayalam — perfectly describing the mist that fills the gorge for 200 metres around the falls.

places.name: Nyayamakad Waterfall
places.description: Kerala's highest single-drop waterfall at 1600m — a vertical plunge through shola forest found only by adventurous trekkers. No tourist infrastructure exists and the 3km forest trail to the falls feels like true exploration.

places.name: Carmelagiri Elephant Park
places.description: A small, responsible elephant park near Munnar where visitors can interact with trained elephants, learn about their care, bathe them in the river and understand Kerala's deep cultural bond with elephants through mahout demonstrations.

places.name: Pallivasal Waterfalls & Heritage Dam
places.description: The site of Kerala's first hydroelectric project (1940), Pallivasal Dam is surrounded by gorgeous forest and fed by a dramatic waterfall. The heritage significance, forest trails and absolute solitude make this a special find.

places.name: Vattavada Vegetable Village
places.description: A remote high-altitude village at 2000m near Munnar known for growing exotic vegetables — garlic, carrots, leeks and cabbage — in freezing mountain fields. The village offers a unique agri-tourism experience entirely off the tourist map.

places.name: Mannavanshola Sacred Forest
places.description: An ancient sacred grove near Rajamala protecting a pristine patch of shola forest untouched for centuries by virtue of its sacred status. The rare plants, ancient trees and silence within the grove feel otherworldly.

places.name: Tea Museum, Munnar (KDHP)
places.description: The story of Munnar's tea industry in an engaging museum run by the Kannan Devan Hills Plantation Company. Century-old machinery, colonial-era photographs and the history of how British planters transformed these hills are wonderfully presented.

places.name: Anamudi Peak — Highest in South India
places.description: South India's highest peak at 2695m, Anamudi rises dramatically above the Eravikulam plateau. Trekking permits are strictly regulated and only given to small groups. The summit view of three states — Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka — is spectacular.

places.name: Anamudi Peak
places.description: The highest peak in South India at 2695m, Anamudi towers over the Eravikulam National Park. The trek to its summit rewards adventurers with stunning 360-degree views of the Western Ghats, shola forests and endemic wildlife.

places.name: Rajamala Hills
places.description: Part of Eravikulam National Park, Rajamala's grassy highlands at 2000m are the primary habitat of the endangered Nilgiri Tahr. The rolling meadows shrouded in mist with panoramic mountain views make this one of Kerala's most scenic spots.

districts.name: Wayanad
districts.description: A lush green highland district with dense forests, waterfalls, and tribal heritage.

places.name: Chembra Peak
places.description: The highest peak in Wayanad at 2100m, Chembra Peak is famous for a heart-shaped lake near the summit. The challenging trek through shola forests offers stunning views of the Nilgiri Hills, and the cloud-covered summit is a magical experience.

places.name: Edakkal Caves
places.description: Ancient natural caves at 1200m containing prehistoric petroglyphs and pictorial writings dating back to the Neolithic Age. These are considered among the earliest evidence of human habitation in South India.

places.name: Pookode Lake
places.description: A freshwater lake nestled amidst evergreen forests at 770m altitude. Pedal boating on the tranquil lake with the forested hills as backdrop is serene. A children's park and aquarium add to the family appeal.

places.name: Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary
places.description: Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, this sanctuary is home to elephants, tigers, leopards, and the rare Asiatic wild dog. Tribal communities have lived here for centuries and their settlements are part of the eco-tourism circuit.

places.name: Soochipara Waterfalls
places.description: A three-tiered waterfall tumbling 200 feet through dense tropical forest. The trek to the falls is scenic with streams and wildlife sightings. The natural pool at the base is perfect for a refreshing dip.

places.name: Phantom Rock Viewpoint
places.description: A dramatic rock formation resembling a human face when viewed from a distance. The viewpoint at Kalpetta offers stunning sunrise and sunset views over Wayanad valleys.

places.name: Banasura Sagar Dam
places.description: India's largest earth dam surrounded by a cluster of hillocks and lush forests. Offers boat rides, island trekking and camping in one of Wayanad's most scenic settings.

places.name: Thirunelli Temple
places.description: An ancient Vishnu temple from the 13th century nestled in dense forests at 900m altitude. Surrounded by the Papanashini River and forested hills, it is called the Kashi of Kerala.

places.name: Muthanga Wildlife Sanctuary
places.description: A 345 sq km forest reserve on the Karnataka border with jeep safari through teak forests. Spot elephants, sambar deer, wild boar and if lucky, a tiger or leopard.

places.name: Kuruva Dweep (Island)
places.description: A protected river island formed by the Kabani River, Kuruva Dweep is accessible only by bamboo rafts. The uninhabited island is covered in rare orchids, bamboo groves and endemic bird species. One of India's most pristine river islands.

places.name: Pakshipathalam Bird Sanctuary
places.description: A secret bird sanctuary in the Brahmagiri Hills, accessible via a challenging 7km trek. Home to over 200 species of birds including the rare Malabar Trogon. Cave shelters used by ancient humans add archaeological intrigue.

places.name: Soochipara (Sentinel Rock) Waterfalls
places.description: A dramatic three-tiered waterfall crashing down from 200 metres into a natural pool surrounded by tropical forest. The trek to the falls passes through coffee and cardamom estates. Swimming is permitted in the lower pools.

places.name: Edakkal Caves (Extended Trail)
places.description: Beyond the famous main chambers of Edakkal Caves lie lesser-known trails through the Ambukuthi Hills leading to secret rock formations and additional petroglyph panels that most tourists never reach. A true hidden heritage trail.

places.name: Karapuzha Dam & Reservoir
places.description: Kerala's largest earthen dam, surrounded by lush forest with almost no tourist development. Boating on the reservoir offers spectacular views of the Wayanad hills. The surrounding forested shores are home to elephants.

places.name: Glass Temple, Sulthan Bathery
places.description: A 13th-century Jain temple hewn from solid rock near Sulthan Bathery, hidden behind a market and completely overlooked by tourists despite being 800 years old. The carved stone pillars and Jain iconography are exceptional.

places.name: Chembra Heart-shaped Lake
places.description: Perched at 2100m on Chembra Peak, this perfectly heart-shaped natural lake has never dried up in recorded history. The 6km trek to reach it through shola forest and rolling grasslands is one of Kerala's most popular adventures.

places.name: Neelimala Viewpoint & Meenmutty Falls
places.description: A breathtaking viewpoint above the Meenmutty Waterfall — Kerala's second highest at 300m. The 2km walk to the falls involves three river crossings and descents into a jungle gorge. The viewpoint above sees almost no visitors.

places.name: Tipu Sultan's Bathery Fort
places.description: The crumbling remains of Tipu Sultan's ammunition storehouse (Bathery = Battery/Arsenal) in the heart of Sulthan Bathery town. This little-visited fort is where the town gets its name, with original stone walls still standing.

places.name: Ambalavayal Heritage Museum
places.description: A remarkable tribal heritage museum showcasing the culture, tools, ornaments and traditions of Wayanad's indigenous Adivasi communities. The museum is run by a tribal self-help group and remains almost entirely off the tourist trail.

places.name: Phantom Rock Sunrise Trek
places.description: A mysterious rock formation above Kalpetta that appears phantom-like in morning mist. The sunrise trek starting at 4am reveals one of Wayanad's most dramatic landscapes — rolling hills emerging from fog below a glowing sky.

places.name: Karlad Lake (Banasurasagar Dam)
places.description: The largest earthen dam in India and second largest in Asia, Banasura Sagar Dam creates a stunning reservoir studded with small islands. Motorboat and speed boat rides weave between the islands with the Banasura Hills as backdrop.

places.name: Meenmutty Falls Full Trek
places.description: Kerala's second highest waterfall at 300m requires a 4km trek with three river crossings. Most tourists only see the lower tier — the full trek to the top reveals two more hidden cascades accessible to almost no one.

places.name: Muthanga Elephant Safari
places.description: Jeep safaris through the Muthanga Wildlife Sanctuary at dawn offer extraordinary wildlife encounters. The sanctuary is the Wayanad section of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve and elephant herds of 50+ animals are regularly spotted.

places.name: Lakkidi Ghat Pass
places.description: At 700m, Lakkidi is Kerala's wettest point and gateway to Wayanad. The misty ghat pass with its perpetual cloud cover, dense forests, chain tree legend and hairpin bends is a magical entry into one of Kerala's coolest districts.

places.name: Vythiri Hill Resort Zone
places.description: A scenic highland zone at 900m surrounded by coffee and pepper plantations, Vythiri offers a cool, misty retreat with treetop cottages, zip-lining and nature walks. The gentle hills and aromatic spice farms create a uniquely relaxing cold-climate experience.

districts.name: Thrissur
districts.description: The cultural capital of Kerala, famous for Thrissur Pooram and ancient temples.

places.name: Thrissur Pooram Ground
places.description: The venue of Kerala's grandest temple festival, Thrissur Pooram. The Thekkinkadu Maidan hosts the spectacular procession of caparisoned elephants, percussion orchestras (Panchavadyam), and dazzling fireworks that draw lakhs of visitors every Medam month.

places.name: Athirappilly Waterfalls
places.description: The largest waterfall in Kerala, Athirappilly Falls (80 feet wide, 80 feet tall) is often called the 'Niagara of India'. Set in the Sholayar forest range, it's the filming location for several Malayalam blockbusters.

places.name: Kerala Kalamandalam
places.description: A Deemed University for traditional performing arts, Kalamandalam is the premier institution for Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Koodiyattam, and other classical art forms. Evening performances and studio visits are available for tourists.

places.name: Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple
places.description: One of the most important Hindu pilgrimage centers in India, Guruvayur Temple is dedicated to Lord Guruvayurappan (Krishna). The temple elephants (Anakkotta) are a unique attraction. The temple follows strict dress codes.

places.name: Snehatheeram Beach (Chavakkad)
places.description: A clean and picturesque beach developed as a tourism hotspot with facilities like boat rides, beach volleyball, and food stalls. The serene atmosphere and beautiful sunsets make it a popular local escape.

places.name: Peechi Dam & Wildlife Sanctuary
places.description: A scenic dam surrounded by dense forests forming part of a wildlife sanctuary. Home to deer, elephants and 200+ bird species. Offers boat rides and a small children's park.

places.name: Shakthan Thampuran Palace
places.description: An 18th-century palace built by the ruler of Kochi with a mix of Kerala and Dutch architectural styles. Houses a collection of ancient artifacts, weapons and royal regalia.

places.name: Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Academy
places.description: The premier institution for performing arts in Kerala, hosting regular classical music, dance and theatre performances. The amphitheater is architecturally spectacular.

places.name: Vazhachal Forest & Waterfalls
places.description: A dense eco-tourism forest adjacent to Athirappilly with the beautiful Charpa Falls and numerous nature trails. Elephants frequently cross the Chalakudy River here.

places.name: Parambikulam Tiger Reserve
places.description: One of India's best-managed tiger reserves, Parambikulam is a biodiversity hotspot with tigers, elephants, bison, leopards and the oldest teak tree on Earth — the Kannimara Teak. Bamboo rafting, guided jungle treks and tribal village stays are available at very affordable rates.

places.name: Cheraman Juma Masjid
places.description: Believed to be India's first mosque, built in 629 AD by Cheraman Perumal who converted to Islam. The mosque features a unique blend of Kerala Hindu temple and Islamic architectural styles with a traditional lamp room, oil lamps and a tank — a remarkable symbol of communal harmony.

places.name: Thrissur Round & Swaraj Round
places.description: The iconic 1-km circular road around the Vadakkumnathan Temple complex is the heart of Thrissur city and venue of the world-famous Thrissur Pooram festival. The surrounding bazaar streets, antique shops, gold market and traditional sweet stalls make for an immersive cultural walk.

places.name: Porkulam Dolmens & Megalithic Sites
places.description: Thrissur district hides ancient megalithic dolmens — prehistoric burial chambers from 1000 BC — scattered across its paddy fields and hillsides. The Porkulam site near Irinjalakuda is one of the most accessible and best-preserved, offering a fascinating glimpse into Kerala's pre-historic civilisation.

places.name: Chal Beach & Kole Wetlands
places.description: Chal Beach near Kodungallur is a quiet, unspoilt beach backed by the Kole Wetlands — a Ramsar-designated waterbird habitat and one of Asia's largest bird sanctuaries. Over 200 migratory bird species arrive between October and February, making this a paradise for nature lovers on a budget.

places.name: Sholayar Dam & Forest
places.description: A remote dam in the upper reaches of Chalakudy River with a restricted-access forest area. The surrounding teak and bamboo forests are pristine and elephant movement is common. Very few tourists reach this area.

places.name: Peechi Reservoir & Dam
places.description: A tranquil reservoir 23 km from Thrissur with a surrounding wildlife sanctuary. The jungle trails offer sightings of deer, monitor lizards and exotic birds. The reservoir is popular with local anglers and picnickers.

places.name: Peringottukurissi Fort
places.description: A largely forgotten 17th-century fort hidden in the foothills of Peringottukurissi village. Built by Haider Ali, the partially ruined fort has secret underground passages and offers panoramic views of the surrounding countryside.

places.name: Chettuva Backwaters
places.description: A hidden backwater estuary north of Thrissur where freshwater rivers meet the Arabian Sea. The mangrove-lined channels, migratory birds and fishing villages are virtually unknown to tourists from outside Kerala.

places.name: Kalamandalam Kathakali & Koodiyattam Centre
places.description: The world's only dedicated institution for preserving Kerala's classical performing arts, UNESCO-recognised Koodiyattam and Kathakali. Students spend 6-10 years mastering these arts. Morning rehearsals are open to visitors.

places.name: Vadakkumnathan Temple
places.description: The oldest and largest Shiva temple in Kerala, situated in the heart of Thrissur. The Thrissur Pooram — India's greatest elephant festival — is held here annually. The temple's ancient murals depicting Mahabharata scenes are priceless.

places.name: Irinjalakuda Natyagramam
places.description: A tiny village near Thrissur that is the birthplace of Koodiyattam — the world's oldest living theatrical tradition and the first performance art to receive UNESCO recognition. The ancient Koodalmanikyam Temple is the epicentre.

places.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Cathedral Thrissur
places.description: The largest church in Kerala and among the top 10 largest churches in Asia, this Indo-Gothic cathedral with its distinctive twin towers is visible from miles around. The underground grotto and massive nave hold 15,000 worshippers.

places.name: Kole Wetlands Bird Sanctuary
places.description: One of Asia's largest wetland ecosystems and a Ramsar site, the Kole wetlands attract over 100,000 migratory birds from Siberia, Europe and Central Asia between October and March. The site is invisible on most tourist maps.

places.name: Chalakudy River Adventure Trail
places.description: The Chalakudy River, which feeds Athirappilly Falls, offers an extraordinary white-water kayaking and rafting route through dense forest. The riverbanks are part of a protected wildlife corridor with hornbills, kingfishers and smooth-coated otters.

places.name: Triprayar Sri Rama Temple
places.description: An extraordinarily ancient Rama temple on the banks of the Triprayar River, featuring one of the five Vishnu temples of Central Kerala known as the Pancha Pandaravaka Kshetrams. The riverside setting and rare Triptych of Rama are unique.

places.name: Guruvayur Devaswom Elephant Sanctuary
places.description: Punnathur Kotta, the elephant sanctuary run by the Guruvayur Devaswom, is home to 60+ elephants dedicated to Lord Guruvayurappan. The largest captive elephant collection in the world. Visitors can walk among the elephants in the morning.

places.name: Paramekkavu Bagavathy Temple
places.description: One of the two main temples that compete during the legendary Thrissur Pooram — one of the world's greatest festivals. The Paramekkavu side's elephant procession, percussion ensemble and parasol competition are breathtaking displays of Kerala tradition.

places.name: Kunnamkulam Traditional Timber Trade Heritage
places.description: The ancient timber trading town of Kunnamkulam has preserved its 200-year-old timber merchant havelis (nalukettu homes) intact. The traditional woodwork, carved wooden boxes and teak-trading heritage are extraordinary and completely overlooked.

places.name: Thrissur Ada Pradaman Heritage
places.description: Thrissur is the heartland of Kerala's most celebrated dessert — Ada Pradaman, a rich payasam of rice flakes cooked in reduced coconut milk and jaggery. The traditional preparation here follows ancient temple-kitchen methods and is served during festivals at the city's famous Vadakkunnathan Temple.
places.best_time: All year (special during Vishu, Thrissur Pooram)

places.name: Irinjalakuda Snack Trail
places.description: A small town near Thrissur famous for its unique local snacks: kaayada (sweet riceflour diamonds), achappam (rosette cookies), and the legendary Irinjalakuda jackfruit chips. The town's traditional tea shops and snack vendors have preserved recipes unchanged for over a century.

places.name: Punnayurkulam Backwater Circuit
places.description: A little-known backwater zone in coastal Thrissur, Punnayurkulam offers quiet canal cruises through fishing villages, coconut plantations and traditional toddy shops. The Kole Wetlands nearby are internationally recognised as an Important Bird Area (IBA) with over 100 migratory species.

districts.name: Kozhikode (Calicut)
districts.description: Historic spice trade city with beautiful beaches, forests, and unique Malabar cuisine.

places.name: Kozhikode Beach
places.description: One of the most famous beaches in North Kerala, known for its twin piers, sunset views, and street food. The beach is dotted with food stalls serving Kozhikode's legendary Halwa, Banana Chips, and seafood. The 140-year-old pier is a historical landmark.

places.name: Beypore Beach & Port
places.description: Famous for its traditional Arab dhow building (Uru), Beypore has been a center of maritime trade since ancient times. Watch master craftsmen build these wooden vessels using centuries-old techniques. The beach is also a tranquil escape.

places.name: Tusharagiri Waterfalls
places.description: A group of three waterfalls set amidst dense tropical forests, Tusharagiri offers thrilling rock sliding opportunities and scenic treks. The thunderous Thenpara falls and the White rock waterfall are the main attractions.

places.name: Mananchira Square
places.description: A historic public square surrounding a natural pond (Mananchira) that was the bathing pool of the Zamorin kings. Today it's a beautifully maintained park with cultural programs, musical fountain, and historical significance.

places.name: Kappad Beach
places.description: The historic beach where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498, marking the beginning of Portuguese-Indian trade relations. A monument commemorates this historic event. The beach has rocky outcrops, clear waters, and excellent seafood shacks.

places.name: Pazhassiraja Museum
places.description: A museum dedicated to Kerala Varma Pazhassiraja, the Lion of Kerala who resisted British rule. Displays rare coins, ancient maps, megalithic relics and bronze idols.

places.name: Thusharagiri Trekking Trail
places.description: A popular trekking destination with three spectacular waterfalls — Thenpara, Narikkunnu and Chakkittapara. Trek through dense cardamom and rubber forests with natural pools.

places.name: SM Street (Mittai Theruvu)
places.description: The famous Sweet Street of Kozhikode, legendary for Kozhikodan Halwa, banana chips and traditional snacks sold in century-old shops. A foodie's paradise in the heart of the city.

places.name: Elathur Beach
places.description: A quiet, clean beach north of Kozhikode favored by locals for its calm waters and absence of tourist crowds. Bordered by casuarina groves and ideal for morning walks.

places.name: Beypore Port & Uru Shipyard
places.description: One of the oldest ports in India and the birthplace of the famous Dhow (Uru) wooden ships. The traditional Arab trading vessels are still handcrafted here using ancient techniques passed down for 1500 years. A living piece of maritime history.

places.name: Thusharagiri Waterfalls
places.description: Three stunning waterfalls — Thenpara, Elapara and വaanapara — set in dense evergreen forest. Adventure activities include river trekking, rappelling down the waterfall faces, and bamboo rafting in the pools below.

places.name: Kappad Beach (Vasco da Gama Landing)
places.description: The historic beach where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498, marking his arrival in India. A commemorative monument stands on the beach. The beach itself is tranquil and underdeveloped — a pilgrimage site for history lovers.

places.name: Kadalundi Bird Sanctuary
places.description: A little-known bird sanctuary at the confluence of the Kadalundi River and the sea. Over 60 species of migratory birds including terns, sandpipers and herons winter here. The mangrove islands are accessible by canoe.

places.name: Tali Temple
places.description: A 14th-century Shiva temple in the heart of Kozhikode city, built in traditional Kerala style with exquisite wood carvings. Largely overlooked by tourists, this is one of the finest examples of Kerala temple architecture in the Malabar region.

places.name: Padinharekara Beach
places.description: One of Kozhikode's most secret beaches, accessible only through a narrow path known to locals. The unspoiled shoreline stretches for kilometres with no commercial development. Migratory turtles nest here between December and February.

places.name: Lokanarkave Temple & Sacred Grove
places.description: A supremely ancient forest temple protecting one of Kerala's last intact sacred groves (Kavu). The surrounding forest ecosystem is preserved by the temple's tradition and harbours rare fauna. The deity is a manifestation of the forest itself.

places.name: Peruvannamuzhi Dam & Garden
places.description: A beautiful dam on the Koodaranhi River surrounded by sculpted gardens, boat rides and picnic spots — Kozhikode's best-kept recreational secret. Crocodiles have been spotted in the reservoir and the sunset views are breathtaking.

places.name: Calicut University Botanical Garden
places.description: A sprawling botanical garden on the Calicut University campus containing over 600 plant species, rare medicinal trees and one of the finest collections of orchids in Kerala. Open to the public and almost entirely tourist-free.

places.name: Moppila Bay Fishing Harbour
places.description: The oldest fishing harbour in Malabar, Moppila Bay is where Kerala's Moppila (Muslim) fishing culture is most vividly on display at dawn. The colourful boats, ancient fish auction, and smells of the sea create an extraordinary atmosphere.

places.name: Vellimadukunnu Heritage Fort Ruins
places.description: The almost completely unknown ruins of a Zamorin-era coastal fort on a hill above Kozhikode, offering panoramic views of the city and sea. The crumbling ramparts and buried cannon sites are visited by almost no one.

places.name: Iruvaznhinad Valley Waterfalls
places.description: A remote valley in the Kozhikode hills containing multiple unnamed waterfalls accessible only through forest paths. Local tribal guides lead visitors through rubber and cardamom estates to reach cascades completely unknown to tourism.

places.name: Malabar Culinary Heritage Trail
places.description: Kozhikode is the birthplace of the famous Malabar Biryani, Kozhikodan Halwa and Kallummakkai (mussels). Walking food tours of SM Street, the old mosques' community kitchens and home-cooking experiences reveal one of India's greatest culinary traditions.

places.name: Kozhikode Beach Sunset Pavilions
places.description: The beach promenade of Kozhikode with its twin piers, ancient pavilions and the nightly gathering of thousands of locals at sunset is one of Kerala's most authentic and beautiful urban experiences. Street food stalls serving Kozhikodan Halwa add to the magic.

places.name: Feroke Mosaic Tile Factory Heritage
places.description: Feroke near Kozhikode is the centre of Kerala's traditional mosaic tile industry, producing the hand-cut geometric tiles found in the floors of Kerala's heritage homes for 200 years. Factory tours reveal a dying craft preserved by a handful of artisans.

places.name: Kozhikode Biryani Trail
places.description: Kozhikode Biryani (Malabar Biryani) is arguably India's most aromatic rice dish, cooked with Jeerakasala rice, fried onions, raisins and tender mutton or chicken. The old town's legendary restaurants like Sagar and Rahmath have been serving this biryani for generations.

places.name: Kozhikode Halwa Market
places.description: Kozhikode is the home of India's most famous halwa — a dense, sticky, ghee-laden sweet made from wheat starch, coconut milk, and jaggery. The Sweet Meat Street (Mittai Theruvu) has dozens of shops selling this iconic delicacy in over 30 flavours.

places.name: Kozhikode Seafood Quarter
places.description: The fishing harbour area of Kozhikode is home to some of Kerala's finest seafood experiences. Freshly caught karimeen (pearl spot), seer fish and tiger prawns are cooked in traditional Malabar spice blends at rustic eateries that locals swear by.

districts.name: Palakkad
districts.description: Gateway to Kerala through the Palakkad Gap, known for forts, forests, and rivers.

places.name: Palakkad Fort
places.description: An 18th-century granite fort built by Hyder Ali, later captured by the British East India Company. The remarkably preserved structure features a moat, bastions, and a small mosque inside. It's one of the best-preserved forts in Kerala.

places.name: Silent Valley National Park
places.description: An untouched rainforest and UNESCO World Heritage Site, Silent Valley is home to the endangered Lion-tailed Macaque, tigers, elephants, and rare birds. The Kuntipuzha river flows through this pristine ecosystem.

places.name: Malampuzha Dam & Gardens
places.description: The largest dam in Kerala with expansive gardens, a ropeway, children's park, and fantasy park. The panoramic views of the Western Ghats from the dam are spectacular. Boating and cable car rides add to the experience.

places.name: Nelliyampathy Hills
places.description: A serene hill station at 1574m known for its coffee, cardamom, and orange plantations. The hairpin bends along the ghat road, misty valleys, and quiet forest paths make Nelliyampathy an offbeat alternative to busier hill stations.

places.name: Pothundy Reservoir
places.description: A beautiful reservoir surrounded by tea and coffee estates, offering a tranquil escape. The boat club and fishing opportunities make it popular with nature lovers seeking off-the-beaten-path destinations.

places.name: Dhoni Waterfalls
places.description: A beautiful 25-meter waterfall hidden inside a forest reserve accessible by trekking. The trek passes through rubber and teak plantations with a refreshing natural pool at the base.

places.name: Kalpathy Heritage Village
places.description: A 500-year-old Brahmin agraharam (village) with traditional Tamil Brahmin architecture. The annual Ratholsavam chariot festival draws thousands and has been listed by UNESCO.

places.name: Toovapara Valley View
places.description: A stunning viewpoint overlooking the Silent Valley core zone with misty forest valleys as far as the eye can see. One of the least-visited but most scenic spots in Palakkad.

places.name: Parambikulam Tiger Reserve
places.description: One of the best-managed tiger reserves in India with rare teak trees (Kannimara teak, 3000 years old), elephants, tigers and bamboo forests. Excellent eco-tourism facilities.

places.name: Malampuzha Garden & Ropeway
places.description: A beautifully landscaped garden beside the Malampuzha reservoir with a ropeway offering aerial views of the dam and the Palakkad Gap. Features a fantasy park, snake park, and one of the few ropeways in Kerala.

places.name: Nenmara-Vallangi Vela Festival Ground
places.description: A remarkable twin village that hosts one of Kerala's most spectacular but least-known temple festivals, Nenmara Vallangi Vela. The elephant processions and fireworks rival Thrissur Pooram but attract far fewer visitors.

places.name: Kalpathy Rathotsavam Heritage Village
places.description: A living 500-year-old Tamil Brahmin village in the heart of Palakkad, granted heritage status by the Government of India. The annual Kalpathy Chariot Festival is the oldest and longest-running chariot festival in Kerala.

places.name: Nelliyampathy Tea & Coffee Estates
places.description: A stunning hill range 60km from Palakkad where tea and coffee estates tumble down misty slopes and the views of the Palakkad plains below are jaw-dropping. Far less visited than Munnar but equally scenic, Nelliyampathy is Palakkad's best-kept secret.

places.name: Meenvallam Waterfalls
places.description: A thundering waterfall set deep in the Parambikulam buffer zone forests, reachable via a 4km jungle trail from the nearest village. The falls drop in three tiers through ancient forest. Known only to local trekkers and forest officials.

places.name: Palakkad Gap — Natural Wind Corridor
places.description: The Palakkad Gap is a unique 24km natural break in the Western Ghats, historically the most important land route between Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Windmills now harness the constant winds, and the geological significance of the Gap is extraordinary.

places.name: Kollengode Palace
places.description: A magnificent 17th-century palace of the Vencayil family — Kerala's most architecturally pure Nalukettu palace still in private hands. Visitors can tour the opulent interior with its rosewood carvings, antique artefacts and sacred family temple.

places.name: Ponnani Lighthouse & Beach
places.description: The historic port town of Ponnani — once the largest port in Kerala — has a colonial lighthouse and a wild, untouched beach that sees almost no tourists. The old mosques and Portuguese-era buildings of the town create a fascinating heritage trail.

places.name: Seethargundu Viewpoint
places.description: A completely secret hilltop viewpoint above Nelliyampathy with an unobstructed 180° view of the Palakkad plains, the Gap, and on clear days the distant Eastern Ghats of Tamil Nadu. Known only to local tea estate workers.

places.name: Attappady Tribal Villages
places.description: A remote highland valley where three indigenous tribes — Muduga, Kurumba and Irular — have lived for millennia. Attappady's tribal homesteads, bamboo crafts, forest medicine and traditional agriculture offer extraordinary cultural immersion.

places.name: Mangalam Dam Reservoir
places.description: A scenic but largely unvisited dam on the Gayathripuzha River with the Agali tribal highlands in the background. The reservoir is fringed with forest and boating here at dawn with mist rising from the water is extraordinary.

places.name: Malampuzha Dam & Fantasy Park
places.description: Set against the backdrop of the Malampuzha Hills, this picturesque dam garden at 500m altitude offers cooler temperatures than the plains. The rope-way to the hilltop, sculptor Kanai Kunhiraman's famous yakshi statue and Fantasy Park create a unique blend of nature and leisure.

places.name: Palakkad Iyer Vegetarian Cuisine Trail
places.description: Palakkad's Tamil Brahmin (Iyer) community has preserved a distinct vegetarian cuisine for centuries. Mor Kuzhambu (buttermilk curry), Paruppu Payasam, Ellu Kozhukatta (sesame dumplings) and the unique Palakkad-style Sambar are culinary treasures unavailable elsewhere.

districts.name: Alappuzha (Alleppey)
districts.description: Venice of the East — backwaters, houseboats, beaches and the famous snake boat races.

places.name: Alleppey Houseboat (Kettuvallam)
places.description: The iconic Kerala houseboat experience. Kettuvallam (traditional rice boats converted to luxury houseboats) glide through the tranquil backwaters past paddy fields, coconut groves, and quaint villages. An overnight cruise is the highlight of any Kerala visit.

places.name: Vembanad Lake
places.description: The longest lake in India stretching 96km, Vembanad Lake is the setting for the famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race. The vast expanse of water fringed with coconut palms is home to migratory birds and a thriving fishing community.

places.name: Krishnapuram Palace
places.description: A beautiful example of Kerala's traditional architecture with gabled roofs, dormer windows, and narrow corridors. The palace houses murals, sculptures, antique furniture, and a large painting of the Gajendra Moksham.

places.name: Marari Beach
places.description: A pristine, uncrowded beach known for its calm waters, clean sands, and traditional fishing village atmosphere. A perfect alternative to busier beaches, Marari offers serenity and a genuine glimpse into Kerala coastal life.

places.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
places.description: Located on the banks of Vembanad Lake, this sanctuary is a haven for rare migratory birds from Siberia, including the Siberian Crane. Canoe rides through narrow waterways offer close-up wildlife encounters amidst dense mangroves.

places.name: Pathiramanal Island
places.description: A tiny mystical island in Vembanad Lake accessible only by boat. Home to over 50 species of rare migratory birds and surrounded by dense green shrubbery. No vehicles allowed.

places.name: Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna Temple
places.description: A 15th-century temple famous for the Palpayasam (rice pudding) prasadam offered daily. According to legend, the recipe originates from a chess game between Krishna and a sage.

places.name: Arthunkal Beach & Church
places.description: A serene beach fronting the historic St. Andrew's Basilica (1584 AD) — a major Christian pilgrimage site. The annual Arthunkal Perunnal festival draws lakhs of devotees.

places.name: Chettikulangara Temple
places.description: Famous for its spectacular Bharani festival where hundreds of decorated wooden elephants (kuthira) are displayed. A unique Kerala tradition not seen anywhere else in the world.

places.name: Nehru Trophy Boat Race Venue
places.description: The finishing point of the world-famous Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race, held every second Saturday of August on Punnamada Lake. Even outside race season, the lake is spectacular for early morning kayaking, watching traditional snake boats practice, and sunset photography from the shore.

places.name: Revi Karuna Museum & Art Gallery
places.description: A remarkable private museum in Alleppey housing over 4,000 artefacts including ancient clocks, furniture, porcelain, silver, paintings, and the world's finest collection of antique Kerala oil lamps. Set in a beautifully restored colonial building, this is one of Kerala's most underrated cultural gems.

places.name: Kuttanad Below Sea Level Farms
places.description: Kuttanad is the only place in Asia where farming is done below sea level — 2 metres beneath the Arabian Sea. Explore this unique agricultural landscape by bicycle or country boat, passing through paddy fields framed by water on all sides, coconut groves and traditional farming villages.

places.name: Ambalapuzha Sri Krishna Temple
places.description: A 15th-century temple on the Alleppey backwaters famous for its 'Palpayasam' (sweetened rice pudding), offered as prasad daily as part of a legendary promise to Lord Krishna. The annual Ambalapuzha Utavam festival draws hundreds of thousands of devotees.

places.name: Alleppey Lighthouse & Beach Park
places.description: The historic Alleppey Lighthouse (1862) stands 30 metres tall near Alleppey Beach. Climb to the top for panoramic views over the Arabian Sea and backwaters. The adjacent beach park with shaded walks, food stalls and local fishing boats makes for a very pleasant afternoon.

places.name: Arthunkal Church (St. Sebastian)
places.description: A 400-year-old Portuguese church built in 1581 on the Arthunkal beach. This hidden coastal church is one of the most important Catholic pilgrimage sites in South India, attracting thousands during the January festival.

places.name: Mararikulam Beach
places.description: A pristine, relatively undiscovered beach village where traditional fishermen outnumber tourists. The coconut-grove-fringed white sand beach and the authentic fishing village lifestyle have been preserved perfectly.

places.name: Punnamada Lake — Nehru Trophy Race Venue
places.description: The venue of the world-famous Nehru Trophy Boat Race held every second Saturday of August. The massive snake boats (Chundan Vallam) can be 100+ feet long and carry 100 oarsmen. One of India's most spectacular sporting events.

places.name: Chettikulangara Bhagavathy Temple
places.description: A famous goddess temple known for its extraordinary Kuthiyottam festival where thousands of devotees pierce their skin with needles as an act of devotion. The Chettikulangara Kettukazhcha — giant illuminated floats — is a breathtaking spectacle.

places.name: Alappuzha Beach & Old Pier
places.description: The 150-year-old pier extending into the Arabian Sea is Alleppey's most iconic landmark, built by the British in 1862. The adjacent beach with its old lighthouse, promenade and evening markets captures the colonial-era charm of this 'Venice of the East'.

places.name: Kavalam Backwater Village
places.description: The birthplace of the Vallam Kali tradition and home to the oldest snake boat in Kerala, Kavalam is a living museum of backwater culture. The village church, snake boat shed and ancient Tharakan family palace are extraordinary finds.

places.name: Rameswaram Island Backwaters
places.description: A tiny island in the middle of the Vembanad Lake accessible by a hand-pulled chain ferry. The island has no motor vehicles, a single road, ancient churches and fishermen who have lived here for centuries. A true backwater secret.

places.name: Champakulam Moolam Boat Race
places.description: The oldest snake boat race in Kerala, predating the Nehru Trophy by centuries. Held on the Pampa River at Champakulam during Karkidakam (July), the traditional boats are ceremonially blessed at the ancient Champakulam Church before the race.

places.name: Pallana Backwater Village
places.description: A secret backwater village accessible only by country boat from Alleppey, where the canal is so narrow that leaves from overhanging trees brush the boat. The village has no electricity after 9pm and the night sky is extraordinary.

places.name: Kainakary Houseboat Village
places.description: The village where Arundhati Roy set her Booker Prize novel 'The God of Small Things'. The pickle factory, the Kottayam family home, the ancient ferry crossing and the backwater landscape are all recognisable from the novel.

places.name: Alleppey Karimeen & Backwater Cuisine
places.description: Alleppey's backwater villages are the birthplace of Kerala's most iconic fish dish — Karimeen Pollichathu (pearl spot fish marinated in red chilli, wrapped in banana leaf and slow-cooked). Houseboat kitchens and lakeshore restaurants serve this dish at its authentic best.

places.name: Kuttanad — Below Sea Level Rice Fields
places.description: Kuttanad is the only place in Asia where farming is done 1.2–3 metres below sea level, creating an extraordinary landscape of paddy fields enclosed by earthen bunds in the middle of backwater lakes. The boat ride through this unique agricultural backwater zone is unlike anywhere else on earth.

places.name: Champakulam Backwater Village
places.description: A sleepy backwater village on a network of canals in Kuttanad, Champakulam is home to the oldest snake boat race in Kerala (since 1956) and the remarkable Champakulam Church — accessible only by boat. The narrow village canals lined with coir factories and toddy shops are quintessential backwater Kerala.

places.name: Punnamada Lake & Nehru Trophy Venue
places.description: The venue of Kerala's most spectacular annual event — the Nehru Trophy Boat Race held every second Saturday of August. The vast Punnamada Lake with its 100+ oared snake boats (Chundan Vallam) charging through cheering crowds is one of India's most electrifying spectacles.

districts.name: Kannur
districts.description: Land of looms and lores — famous for Theyyam, forts, and pristine beaches.

places.name: St. Angelo Fort
places.description: Built by the Portuguese in 1505 CE, St. Angelo Fort is one of the oldest forts in Kerala. Located on a rocky promontory overlooking the Arabian Sea, it offers magnificent ocean views and a glimpse into Kerala's colonial maritime history.

places.name: Theyyam Ritual Performances
places.description: Theyyam is a ritualistic dance form considered one of India's most spectacular folk art traditions. Performers with elaborate costumes, towering headgear, and fiery make-up embody deities. Over 400 Theyyam forms exist, each with its own costume and mythology.

places.name: Muzhappilangad Drive-In Beach
places.description: Asia's longest drive-in beach stretching 4km, where vehicles can drive on the hard sand. The golden beach with coconut palms and a small island (Dharmadom) visible offshore is a unique and thrilling experience.

places.name: Parassinikadavu Snake Farm
places.description: A popular tourist spot combining a snake park with the famous Parassinikkadavu Sri Muthappan Temple, known for its unique ritual Theyyam performed daily. The snake park houses numerous rare species.

places.name: Ezhimala Hills & Beach
places.description: A promontory featuring both hills and a beautiful beach, Ezhimala is the site of India's prestigious Naval Academy. The natural harbor, dense forests, and beautiful shoreline make it an exceptional destination.

places.name: Arakkal Museum
places.description: The only Muslim royal family museum in Kerala, housed in the 18th-century Arakkal Palace. Displays ancient weapons, crockery, royal documents and coins from the maritime Muslim kingdom.

places.name: Meenkunnu Beach
places.description: A pristine, uncrowded beach with golden sand and calm blue waters, lined with coconut palms. Rarely visited by tourists, making it a perfect peaceful escape from busy beaches.

places.name: Fort St. Angelo Detailed Tour
places.description: Built by the Portuguese in 1505, this laterite fort with 10m high walls commands sweeping views of Kannur harbor. Well-preserved with old cannons, bastions and barracks still intact.

places.name: Dharmadom Island
places.description: A small island in the Mappila Bay surrounded by the Kanjiramattom River, accessible by canoe. Ringed by casuarina forests and linked to the history of Tipu Sultan's army.

places.name: Ezhimala Hill & Naval Academy
places.description: A sacred hill at the tip of the Malabar Coast with ancient Buddhist ruins and panoramic views of the Arabian Sea. The hill is home to the Indian Naval Academy and the scenic drive around it is spectacular. Limited tourist access makes it exclusive.

places.name: Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary
places.description: Kerala's northernmost wildlife sanctuary bordering Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, Aralam harbours tigers, elephants and the extremely rare Malabar civet. The sanctuary is managed by an agricultural farm and receives very few visitors.

places.name: Payyambalam Beach
places.description: A long, serene beach in Kannur town with a beautiful sculpture park along the promenade. Preferred by locals over the crowded tourist beaches, this peaceful stretch offers excellent sunrise views and a lovely public garden.

places.name: Muzhappilangad Drive-in Beach
places.description: Asia's longest drive-in beach stretching 4km, where vehicles can drive on the hard sand. The unique experience of driving with waves crashing beside you at sunset is unforgettable. Popular but spacious enough to feel uncrowded.

places.name: Anjarakandy Spice Estate
places.description: A historic 200-year-old colonial spice estate hidden in Kannur's hills, producing pepper, cardamom, clove and vanilla. Guided walks through the estate reveal the traditional cultivation methods unchanged since British times.

places.name: Theyyam Performance Villages (North Malabar)
places.description: Kannur is the homeland of Theyyam — Kerala's most spectacular ritual art form where performers become divine incarnations through elaborate costumes and trance states. The real performances happen in remote village temples October to May, not in staged shows.

places.name: Fort St. Angelo
places.description: A magnificent Portuguese fort built in 1505 — one of the oldest European forts in India. Overlooking the Mappila Bay, the fort was controlled successively by the Portuguese, Dutch and British. The panoramic views of the harbour and Laccadive Sea are stunning.

places.name: Azhikkal Lighthouse & Beach
places.description: A perfectly isolated lighthouse on a river-mouth peninsula where the Valapattanam River meets the sea. The beach on both sides of the lighthouse is wild and deserted, with fishermen's boats the only company at sunrise.

places.name: Parassinikadavu Sri Muthappan Temple
places.description: A unique and ancient temple where the deity Muthappan is worshipped through toddy and dried fish offerings — entirely unlike conventional Hindu temples. The daily Theyyam performance here is one of the only daily Theyyam rituals in the world.

places.name: Kavvayi Backwaters
places.description: The largest network of backwaters in North Kerala, Kavvayi covers an area of 14 sq km with numerous islands, mangrove channels and bird habitats. Far less visited than Alleppey, this is Kerala's northern backwater secret.

places.name: Tellicherry Fort & Spice Town
places.description: A 1708 British fort in Thalassery (Tellicherry) that was the birthplace of circus arts in India and the place where the British first cultivated pepper commercially. The fort's bastion views, old British cemetery and spice market are fascinating.

places.name: Ezhara Beach & Lighthouse Walk
places.description: A pristine 7km continuous beach north of Kannur connecting several fishing villages, accessed via a lighthouse walk virtually unknown to tourists. The entire stretch has no development, only fishing boats and the occasional toddy shop.

places.name: Iritty Coffee & Pepper Trail
places.description: The hills around Iritty in north Kannur are covered in coffee, pepper and cardamom estates, cut through by forest streams and waterfalls. Estate walks here are completely off the tourist map despite being among Kerala's most beautiful highland landscapes.

places.name: Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary Highlands
places.description: The northernmost wildlife sanctuary in Kerala, Aralam's highlands rise to 1145m and stay refreshingly cool year-round. This under-visited sanctuary shelters elephants, leopards, sloth bears and the rare Malabar giant squirrel in pristine forest.

places.name: Paithalmala Peak
places.description: At 1190m, Paithalmala is Kannur's highest peak and one of Kerala's most scenic trekking destinations. The grassland summit offers 360-degree views of Coorg in Karnataka and the Arabian Sea, while the ascent passes through pristine shola forests.

places.name: Thalassery Biryani & Malabar Kitchen
places.description: Thalassery Biryani is a distinct style unique to this North Kerala town — using fragrant Kaima rice, ghee-fried cashews, boiled eggs and Malabar spices. The old town's legendary Moosakutty Hotel and surrounding street stalls serve this biryani in its most authentic form.

places.name: Kannur Traditional Sweets Trail
places.description: North Kerala's traditional sweets are masterpieces of rice and coconut artistry. Pazham Nirachath (banana stuffed with coconut and jaggery), Nei Appam (ghee rice pancakes), Kozhukatta (steamed rice dumplings) and Unniappam are local specialties found in Kannur's old market areas.

places.name: Valiyaparamba Backwaters
places.description: North Kerala's finest backwater destination, Valiyaparamba consists of four rivers meeting the sea amid a cluster of uninhabited islands. Far less touristy than Alleppey, the serenity, the cashew-forested islands and the traditional fishing culture here is unmatched.

places.name: Kavvayi Island Backwaters
places.description: Kavvayi is the largest river island in Kerala and Asia's second largest, surrounded by a network of backwater channels. The island backwaters are home to crocodiles, otters and sea eagles, navigable by flat-bottomed wooden boats through dense mangrove corridors.

districts.name: Kasaragod
districts.description: Land of seven languages, ancient forts, and beautiful forest-fringed beaches.

places.name: Bekal Fort
places.description: The largest fort in Kerala, Bekal Fort stands 40 feet above sea level offering a breathtaking 360-degree view of the Arabian Sea. Built in 1650 by the Kolathiri rajas, its keyhole-shaped entrance and observation tower are iconic. The adjacent beach is pristine.

places.name: Ananthapura Lake Temple
places.description: The only lake temple in Kerala, Ananthapura is set on a small island in the middle of a natural lake. It's considered the original seat (moolasthanam) of Ananthapadmanabha (the deity of Padmanabhaswamy Temple). A friendly vegetarian crocodile ('Babiya') lives in the temple lake.

places.name: Valiyaparamba Backwaters
places.description: Kerala's northernmost backwaters with four rivers flowing into the Arabian Sea. The island village of Valiyaparamba is accessible only by boat, offering an untouched, authentic backwater experience away from tourist crowds.

places.name: Chandragiri Fort
places.description: A riverside fort offering panoramic views of the Chandragiri River and the Arabian Sea. The serene setting, ancient architecture, and boat rides on the river make it a peaceful historical excursion.

places.name: Malik Deenar Mosque
places.description: One of the oldest mosques in India, built by Malik ibn Dinar, a companion of Prophet Muhammad who brought Islam to Kerala. The ancient structure blends Kerala and Islamic architecture and remains an active place of worship.

places.name: Nityananda Ashram
places.description: A spiritual center set amidst hills and forests with a large meditation hall and beautiful gardens. Followers of Swami Nityananda visit from across the world.

places.name: Kottancherry Hills
places.description: A scenic viewpoint in the Western Ghats offering panoramic views of the Kasaragod coastline and Arabian Sea from 900m altitude. Famous for sunrise and sunset photography.

places.name: Ranipuram (Malabar Ooty)
places.description: Called the Ooty of Malabar, this 750m hill station on the Karnataka border is covered with dense shola forests, grasslands and rich biodiversity. Popular trekking and camping spot.

places.name: Hosdurg Fort
places.description: A lesser-known but well-preserved fort near Kanhangad with a mix of Portuguese and Kerala architectural elements. Inside the fort complex is a palace, tank and a small temple.

places.name: Madhur Maha Ganapathy Temple
places.description: One of Kerala's most celebrated Ganesha temples, perched above the Madhuvahini River. The 10th-century temple features exquisite Kerala woodcarving, unique rituals and the spectacular Madhur Onam festival. The temple tank, sacred grove and riverside setting make it exceptionally scenic.

places.name: Kappil Beach & Kappil Lake
places.description: A pristine, largely undiscovered beach where a palm-fringed freshwater lake meets the Arabian Sea. The narrow strip of land separating lake from sea makes for spectacular views, perfect swimming conditions and incredible photo opportunities. Far less crowded than Kovalam or Varkala.

places.name: Nileshwaram Palace & Town
places.description: The royal town of Nileshwaram was the seat of the Nileshwaram Kovilakom (royal family). Wander through the old palace grounds, centuries-old temples, and the vibrant local market famous for Kasaragod handloom sarees and traditional brassware.

places.name: Ranipuram Hill Trek (Malabar Ooty)
places.description: Called the Ooty of Malabar, Ranipuram sits at 750m amid thick shola forests and grasslands on the Karnataka border. The trek passes through orchid-rich forests, open meadows with stunning 360° views, and tribal settlements. Extremely affordable guided treks are available.

places.name: Bekal Hole Beach & Bekal Fort Walk
places.description: The longest beach in Kerala stretches for 6 km from Bekal Fort to Pallikere. The famous keyhole-shaped viewing platform inside Bekal Fort gives a breathtaking panoramic view of the sea and coast. The beach itself is pristine, uncrowded and ideal for long walks and swimming.

places.name: Ranipuram Trek
places.description: Known as the 'Ooty of Kasaragod', Ranipuram is a high-altitude meadow at 760m accessible via a challenging trek through dense shola forest. The expansive grasslands with misty views and total absence of tourist infrastructure make it extraordinary.

places.name: Kappil Lake & Beach
places.description: A stunning confluence where the Kappil Lake meets the sea at a narrow opening. The lake is fringed with coconut palms and the narrow strip between the lake and sea is perfect for walking. Almost entirely unknown to outside tourists.

places.name: Madhur Maha Ganapathi Temple
places.description: One of the most celebrated Ganapathi temples in South India, Madhur Temple is built over a natural water spring. The 10th-century temple's unique feature is that the deity here is self-manifested (Swayambhu) from a termite mound.

places.name: Gurudev Nityananda Ashram, Kanhangad
